claims.claim: Reviewers report that crafting stations lack a production queue and automatically drop completed items onto the ground, which leads to other players accidentally picking them up in multiplayer.

citations.review_text:
So, by no means I detest the game. I wish there was a "in-between" review because I am mixed on the game. 

The positives: I am having a great time with the friends. Exploring together, gathering resources. You know, the typical survival/build game. I enjoy it. I am not experiencing any crashing. No stuttering. The open world looks beautiful. When the sun rises and you see the foggy mornings, it is actually damn beautiful. 

The negatives: I don't know if I can keep this short. So, every damn goblin, cow and rat ALWAYS have something to say. I wish there was a setting where I can turn it off or make them less annoying. "Yes, I know you are there. No need to scream at me every 5 seconds." I can tune down the SFX but that would literally mute the entire world. I just want them to tone it down a bit. 
The skills you gain from cooking is not very... rewarding? You learn something new every few or so levels. However, it is just decrease burn chance. I have only burnt shrimp once. After that, I have not not burnt anything else. I don't know, but the leveling system for cooking feels boring. 
Also, why do we have to camp to wait for our food to cook or any other crafting or smelting? I was hoping as you level, you cook things faster or in general. Yes, there is a spell to increase cooking speed but I don't like it. Lol. Why do the developers think it is a good idea for the food to spit out after cooking? If my friends accidentally gets the cooked food, I just lost the experience. It just feels artificial from the devs where they want me to be planted and just stare at the screen. Where in other survival games, I can tend to other projects. Big rant, I know. But that is like with almost every skill in this game. Nothing really feels good or rewarding. Aside from blacksmithing and maybe crafting. Also, yes! I am a housewife in these games. Kitchen and tending to my garden. So, what? 
The aggro in the game is just too aggressive. I am having an archer from literally ac…

1. Lack of diversity in class-specific set bonuses. For example, the only difference between the Iron Warrior Set and the Bronze Warrior Set is the defense stat. Even the set crafting recipes obtained from dungeons don't offer any extra set bonuses.

2. The crafting stations lack a production queue. Once an item is crafted, it just drops directly onto the ground. This is incredibly frustrating in multiplayer, as other players often end up accidentally picking up your items.

3. Severe lack of monster variety. You constantly fight the same few enemies: rats, wolves, and goblins. Even the dungeons are filled with identical guards and bosses, which becomes extremely tedious and repetitive later on.

4. The spellbook (Q key) is completely unorganized. Because skills are split by proficiency levels, life skills and weapon enchantments are all jumbled together. The UI looks extremely cluttered and messy.

5. Food buffs are negligible. There are no foods or skills that temporarily increase maximum HP or provide health/stamina regeneration. You are forced to rely solely on Water Magic for healing.

6. Mounts are locked too far into the late game. There are no temporary speed boosts available, making traversing the map a painful and tedious chore.

7. Melee blocking feels terrible. Dodging/rolling is far more effective than blocking, making shields completely useless. You don't feel like you're mitigating any damage even when successfully blocking an attack with a shield.

8. The game feels like a cheap, generic title slapped with a medieval fantasy skin. Many mechanics and systems feel incredibly outdated, and frankly, unacceptable for a game released in 2025/2026.

9. Highly suspect Steam reviews that don't match actual player engagement. The game currently sits at "Overwhelmingly Positive," yet the global achievement stats tell a completely different story. Many simple, early-game achievements that should be easily unlocked within the first hour have completion rates of l…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that combat features animation locking that prevents dodging out of actions, making melee combat feel unresponsive and sluggish.

citations.review_text:
Coming from games such as OSRS, RS3, Valheim, Enshrouded, Core Keeper, and V Rising, RuneScape: Dragonwilds delivers something interesting. Here are my current impressions with 7.2h of playing:

Graphics & environment: Absolutely stunning. Captures the world perfectly.

Story: Somewhat entertaining, but could use more love. While there is no speech audio, which I understand why that might be, I am someone who just skips the dialogue at times.  

Gameplay: Building, crafting, and spells are good and fun. Combat is engaging; however, I want it to be smoother with animations and not lock you in them. Boss mechanics are challenging and fun, including environmental ones. 

Overall impressions: RuneScape: Dragonwilds delivers a fun and engaging experience. I hope there will be further improvements down the line in combat and animations. If you are thinking about jumping in right now and can’t wait until the new update drops, I recommend buying it now or waiting until the new update drops alongside a sale next week. 

Score: 8.5/10

Having played since pre-alpha I cannot recommend this game yet, but will update my review after 1.0.

My biggest gripe is the combat, specifically long animation locking, feels incredibly dull and janky. I spent quite a few corpse runs back to my body after deaths from accidentally clicking one singular time near enemies. Dodging does not cancel animations either.

The second gripe is the current development state of skills and quests which is still missing so much, but 1.0 should address this.

Ironically, a game based off of Runescape is better played with friends rather than solo.

Unfortunately, the game flops pretty hard with combat.  It actually has good bones!  It's not bad! ... But fighting multiple enemies reveals how sloppy it is.  It doesn't help that shields don't actually block damage.  In fact, if you block an attack "perfectly" on time, you'll block it and still somehow take full damage.  I guess that's on their long list of bugs to fix.  Parrying is satisfying, but again, with multiple enemies, parrying multiple melee enemies and archers that chunk 1/3 of your hp per hit doesn't work out well.

As you reach the 3rd area, it's clear that the game wants you to make Teleporters and build multiple homes.  That's fine, but there's too much friction with resources.  Example: I can build a basic bed with coarse animals scraps from the 1st area, but i can't build a bed with soft fur from the 3rd area?  I need Flax flowers, which I can only find in the 1st zone, to build a sewing wheel? Ummm what? These are chores that add nothing of interest to the gameplay.  Wood, stone and basic animal fur should be available in every zone and should be enough to produce all of the basic workbenches.  Conan Exiles nails this!  COPY THEM!

I may play it some more, but I'm not hopeful that it's going to improve much unless I played with a group of people.

I wish I could give a mixed review. It is fun, but it doesn't have enough content. You're definitely not getting nearly as much value for your money as Valheim for instance.

I haven't played RS since I was a kid, I thought we'd level up through the metals, but it stopped at steel. The higher tier metals are what's iconic about RS for me, so that was very disappointing. 

And magic seems so much better than the other fighting types. Ranged is just OK. But using melee weapons besides the dagger feels bad, especially blocking, a single block and all your stamina is just gone. The same stamina bar is used for everything, which I think could use a rework.

The fishing minigame is also pretty lame, I ignored fishing because of it.

I think they should give you a mount earlier in the game, you don't get it until the last area, and by that point I was teleporting everywhere anyways.

I can't recommend this game in its current state.

First, I want to give credit where it's due. For an Early Access game, it actually runs pretty well. I didn't run into many bugs during my time playing. The biggest issue was the audio bug, which is incredibly annoying. After looking into it, I found that it's apparently been in the game since day one, and from what I could find, the developers have chosen not to fix it. That's disappointing, but it's not the reason I'm giving this review.

My biggest problems are with the gameplay itself.

1. Traveling is painfully slow. Even after unlocking a mount, getting around the world feels like it takes forever. Be prepared to have YouTube playing on a second monitor while you travel. The game does let you build an unlimited number of portals, which helps, but most locations are only worth visiting once. After you've cleared an area, there's very little reason to ever go back.

2. Dungeons have almost no replay value. You clear a dungeon, grab what you came for, and you're done. The bosses don't drop anything exciting or worthwhile, so there's little incentive to fight them again. The only real reason to revisit dungeons is to farm cores, and even that can be solved by simply building your base next to one and checking in every few hours.

3. Magic is disappointing. This is probably my biggest complaint. The game has an entire class dedicated to magic, but there are only three real combat spells, and you'll spend almost the entire game using the same two over and over. Combat quickly becomes repetitive, and there just isn't enough variety to make playing a mage feel rewarding.

4. Combat lacks depth. The actual mechanics for melee and archery are solid, and those weapons feel good to use. The problem is that there aren't enough abilities, skills, or combat options to keep things interesting. Once you've experienced the combat for a few hours, you've basically seen everything it has to offer.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe fast travel as dependent on law runes which are locked behind high-level runecrafting, leading to extensive travel across the map.

citations.review_text:
Great game, but fast travel needs some work

I've played around 31 hours of RuneScape: Dragonwilds so far and I'm really enjoying it. The combination of survival, exploration, RuneScape skills and progression works surprisingly well, and there's a lot to do. The world also feels genuinely huge, which makes exploration exciting.

However, the size of the map becomes a bit of a problem because fast travel is so dependent on Law Runes.

For new characters, Law Runes are locked behind level 50 Runecrafting, while teleportation becomes useful much earlier in the game. I'm currently around level 36 after 26 hours, so level 50 still feels quite far away. You can find Law Runes from vents and other sources, but they are still difficult to keep stocked when you're constantly travelling around such a massive map.

I understand that the developers don't want teleportation to completely remove the importance of exploration, but I think there should be a better middle ground. Either make Law Runes more accessible earlier, reduce the teleport cost even further, or introduce some additional fast-travel options.

The map is huge, and that's one of the game's strengths, but at the same time it can turn travelling between areas into a lot of running back and forth. Especially when you have to return to your base, get resources, go back to where you were, and repeat the process.

I'd also like to see more ways of making long-distance travel convenient without completely removing the survival/exploration aspect.

Overall though, I'm having a great time with the game. The world, progression and gameplay loop are really good, and I'm definitely going to keep playing. I just think the fast-travel system could be improved significantly, especially for players who haven't reached 50 Runecrafting yet.

8/10 so far. Great game with a few progression/travel decisions that I think could be improved.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the inventory space is too small, requiring trips back to base.

citations.review_text: Love the game, I turned xp down to half so I can enjoy the ride.  Biggest downfall is the pathetically TINY Inventory.

Fun game.

But :
- Having to enter the in game wiki, to find what mob drops what, takes too much time. It should be directly displayed on the item itself (component and final product).
- The different damage types are on paper interesting, but don't have much impact in reality.
- The inventory is much too small : having to go back and forth every 5 minutes to my base is boring. (Yes, I could only loot what I'm looking for, but I'm a hoarder).
- Mini bosses don't have personnalised drop, would love to have to farm them to get good loot.
- Spells should be more impactful. I see them as ultimates, big kaboom and utility after a long cooldown. Right now most feel like a very small QoL, usable every minute or so. Make them stronger, even if it means longer cooldowns.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that building limitations and rules regarding which cliffs can be built upon are unclear.

citations.review_text:
Great game. Mostly intuitive controls. Good gameplay. Good difficulty progression. Only found a few minor bugs. Only a few minor quality of life issues, most of which I was able to fix via modding (with the help of AI). Very difficult endgame as of now, considering the game isn't finished. Pretty good build system, although unlike games such as Valheim, the build limitations aren't clear (also some bugs in that area).

Overall, this is a great game given its state and I'd recommend it to anyone who likes a good adventure and has the patience to play for 200+ hours.

I'm having so much fun with this but it is still very barebones. 
Hoping it becomes better over time. 
I am absolutely loving the building though. Just wish they'd give us more options. It's weird that some cliffs can be built upon while others are blocked off for no good reason. 
I like building nice looking bridges between small gaps and I'd love to be able to use the cliffsides for supports.
